title: The Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complexes: Structure-based Function and Regulation
authors: Patel MS, Nemeria NS, Furey W, Jordan F
funder: Supported, in whole or in part, by National Institutes of Health grants DK 20478 (to M.S.P.), GM050380 (to F.J.) and GM061791 (to W.F.) and by the Veterans Affairs Merit Review (W.F.).
result: Review. The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex links glycolysis to the tricarboxylic acid cycle and comprises pyruvate dehydrogenase (E1), dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase (E2) and dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (E3), which work sequentially. E1, a thiamin diphosphate-dependent enzyme, decarboxylates pyruvate and reductively acetylates the lipoyl groups covalently attached to E2; E2 transfers the acetyl group to CoA, forming acetyl-CoA; E3 transfers electrons from the dihydrolipoyl groups of E2 to FAD and then to NAD+.
